tasks.setup: A NUTECH email that has never been used on Skilient
tasks.task: You've heard Skilient is a social platform only for university students. On your phone, open skilient.com, work out what it's for, then create your account.
tasks.done: You're asked about your program and batch.
questions: Before you signed up, what did you think Skilient would do for you? Write one sentence.
Was any field in the sign-up form unclear, or did it ask for something you didn't expect? Which one?
How did you know your code was on its way? How long did it take to arrive?
Did you open the User Agreement? What did you expect to find in it?

tasks.setup: Tester from the task before (already has an account)
tasks.task: Try signing up three more times: once with a personal email (like Gmail), once with your university email but a typo in the part after @, and once with the email you already used.
tasks.done: You've seen what Skilient says for each attempt.
questions: Copy what the page said each time. Did it tell you what to do next?
When the email wasn't recognised, did you understand you could ask for your university to be added? Would you bother?
Did any message make you feel you'd done something wrong?
If you were asked to choose your university, was your university's name easy to find?

tasks.setup: A tester who hasn't signed up yet and has a university Google account
tasks.task: Sign up with 'Continue with Google'. Try a personal Google account first, then your university Google account.
tasks.done: You're signed up through Google, or you've seen why you can't be.
questions: Which way of signing up would you normally pick (email or Google), and why?
What did Skilient say about the personal Google account? Was it clear?
After Google, were you asked to confirm anything else? Was that expected?
notes: Google OAuth isn't configured on the local stack; use a university Google Workspace test account.

tasks.task: Make mistakes on purpose while signing up: press sign up without ticking the agreement, use the password 'password1', then 'password123', type a wrong code twice, then open the email link on a different device. Close everything, come back later and sign in.
tasks.done: You've seen each message and finished signing up.
questions: For each mistake, did the message appear next to the right field?
Could you see each message on your phone without scrolling?
How did you get a new code, and how many tries did it take?
What happened when you opened the link on another device, and when you signed in later? Did you know what to do?

tasks.task: Sign out of Skilient. Sign back in without typing your password.
tasks.done: You're back on Skilient, signed in.
questions: How did you find a way in without your password?
Which sign-in method would you use day to day, and why?
After signing in, did you land where you expected?

tasks.task: Sign in with a typo in your password. Then pretend you've forgotten it and get back in with a new one. Open the reset email twice.
tasks.done: You're signed in with your new password.
questions: What did the page say for the wrong password?
How long did recovery take from start to finish?
Did you trust the reset email was really from Skilient? What made you trust or doubt it?
What happened when you opened the reset link the second time?

tasks.setup: Tester installs an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator) first
tasks.task: Turn on two-step sign-in for your account using an authenticator app. Sign out and sign in again.
tasks.done: You've signed in using the authenticator code.
questions: Did Skilient explain why you'd want this?
Which step was hardest?
What would you do if you lost your phone? Does Skilient tell you?

tasks.setup: Team publishes a new User Agreement version before the session
tasks.task: Sign in. If Skilient asks you to do anything before you continue, do it.
tasks.done: You're on Home.
questions: What did Skilient ask you to do, and why?
Did you read 'What changed'? Was it short enough?
Did you feel you had a real choice?

tasks.task: You've just confirmed your email. Set up your profile so classmates can find you. Skip anything you'd rather not do now.
tasks.done: The welcome screen appears.
questions: Under each step's title there's a line saying why it's asked. Which step still felt unnecessary?
Which step did you skip, and why?
If you connected GitHub: on the skills step, what do you think 'L1', 'L2' and 'claimed' mean?
At any point, how many steps did you think were left? Was that right?

tasks.task: Halfway through setting up, close the browser. Open Skilient again and finish. Try a username a friend already uses, and a very large photo.
tasks.done: Setup is finished.
questions: Where did Skilient bring you back to?
What did it say about the taken username? Did it suggest another?
Did going Back lose anything you'd typed?
What happened with the large photo?

tasks.setup: Tester with a GitHub account and at least one repository
tasks.task: During setup, connect your GitHub account and choose which repositories Skilient may read.
tasks.done: You see skills detected from your code.
questions: Before connecting, did you understand what Skilient reads and what it never reads?
How did you feel about letting Skilient into your repositories?
Were the detected skills what you expected? Any missing or wrong?
notes: Needs the GitHub App and the github-worker.

tasks.setup: Ask one tester to turn on 'Reduce motion' in phone settings first
tasks.task: When you reach the welcome screen, decide whether to take the tour.
tasks.done: You're on Home.
questions: What did the welcome screen tell you to expect?
Did you take the tour or skip it? Why?
How did you feel at that moment? One word.
(If 'Reduce motion' is on in your phone settings) Did anything move in a way that bothered you?

tasks.setup: Officer helper adds the tester's university email at a test event's check-in before the tester signs up
tasks.task: A society added you to an event's attendance before you joined Skilient. Use the email you received to sign up, and get that entry.
tasks.done: The entry is on your Record.
questions: Did the email look trustworthy enough to click? Why?
After signing up, how did you find the waiting entry?
What do you think that entry proves, and to whom?
notes: The claim email needs the notify worker. Locally, use the claim card on the welcome screen instead.

tasks.setup: Tester who hasn't taken the tour yet
tasks.task: Take the tour. Then, without looking back, write what Home, Openings, Ventures, Chat and Me are each for.
tasks.done: You've written one line for each area.
questions: Write one line per area.
Which tour step did you skip through without reading?
Was the tour too long, too short, or about right?

tasks.task: Without asking anyone, find what Skilient suggests you do next to improve your standing, and start doing it.
tasks.done: You've started the suggested step.
questions: Where did you find the suggestion?
Did you understand how many points each item gives and what points are for?
Did any checklist item seem impossible for you right now? Which one?

tasks.task: On a computer: find the Skill swap page using only the search at the top (no menus), then your privacy settings the same way. Afterwards, hover over each icon in the left rail.
tasks.done: You've reached both pages and read the rail tooltips.
questions: What did you type to find each page? Did the first try work?
Which rail icons were you unsure about before hovering?
Did the tooltips help you tell the icons apart?

tasks.task: Open three pages you haven't visited yet that show a first-visit tip: Openings, a venture page, your CV, your score or the Privacy centre. Read the tip that appears.
tasks.done: You've seen three new pages.
questions: Did a tip tell you something you didn't know?
On an empty page, was the suggested action the one you'd want?
Did you close a tip? Would you want it back later?

tasks.task: You skipped the tour earlier. Find a way to watch it again. Then hide your getting-started progress for today and find where it went.
tasks.done: The tour is replaying, and you know where your progress went.
questions: Where did you look first for the tour?
How long did it take?
Could you get the checklist back? Did you expect to?

tasks.setup: At least 5 posts of different types at the tester's university. Include posts older than 2 hours (the feed's seed stage), or the tester sees almost none; the pilot seed ages them.
tasks.task: Scroll your University Feed to the end. For each post, answer the question under it honestly.
tasks.done: You reach the end of the feed.
questions: What do you think your tick or cross does? Who sees it?
After you answered, what did the space under the post show? Did it look finished or broken?
Did you miss having a like button? What would you have done instead?
Did any question not fit the post it was under?

tasks.task: Answer a post's question, then change your answer. Come back after 10 minutes and try to change it again.
tasks.done: You know whether you can still change it.
questions: How did you change your answer? Was it obvious you could?
What happened after 15 minutes? Did Skilient say why?
Should answers be changeable? For how long?

tasks.setup: Any signed-in tester. Include posts older than 2 hours (the feed's seed stage), or the tester sees almost none; the pilot seed ages them.
tasks.task: Look only at posts about events, then only Shipped projects. Then switch to the Global Feed.
tasks.done: You've used two filters and both feeds.
questions: How could you tell which filter was on?
In your words, what's the difference between the University and Global feeds?
What did you find in the Global Feed?

tasks.setup: A poll post and a post with a few comments at the tester's university
tasks.task: Vote in a poll. Then read the comments on a post and reply to someone, mentioning them with @.
tasks.done: Your vote and your reply are posted.
questions: When did you see the poll results? Was that what you expected?
Could you tell which comment your reply belongs to?
Did the @mention suggest names as you typed?

tasks.setup: Helper posts '[UX test] report me' at the tester's university
tasks.task: One post isn't for you and one person posts too often: see less of each. Report the post titled '[UX test] report me' first, then mute its author.
tasks.done: You've hidden one post, muted one person and reported the test post.
questions: What do you think 'Not for me' and 'Mute' each do? Is the person told?
Were the report reasons clear?
After reporting, what did you expect to happen, and when?

tasks.task: On a computer, use only the keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc, arrow keys): answer a post's question, open its comments, open its ⋯ menu and close it again.
tasks.done: You've done all three without the mouse.
questions: Could you always see where you were on the page?
Was any control impossible to reach or to leave?
Did the tick and cross say what they do when focused?

tasks.task: Switch your phone between light and dark mode, then set your browser's font size to the largest (Chrome: Settings > Accessibility > Text scaling), then your phone's text size. Browse Home, a venture page and your CV in each.
tasks.done: You've seen all three pages both ways.
questions: Was anything hard to read in either mode?
Did any text get cut off or overlap with large text?
Which mode looked better to you, and why?

tasks.task: Share something useful with students at your university: a short post with one photo. Make sure only your university sees it. Try a very large photo first. Once you've seen what happens with it, remove the big photo so the post has one photo.
tasks.done: Your post is in the feed.
questions: Before posting, who did you think would see it? How did you check?
What happened with the large photo?
After posting, where did your post appear?
Did anything tell you the post worked?

tasks.task: Ask your batch a question as a poll with three options that closes in two days.
tasks.done: Your poll is posted.
questions: Was it clear how to add or remove options?
Where did you set when it closes?
Was there anything you wanted that wasn't there?

tasks.task: Start writing a post, leave Home and come back. Then post twice quickly, and try posting with nothing in it.
tasks.done: You've seen what happens each time.
questions: Was your draft still there? Did you expect it to be?
What happened on the second post? Did it say how long to wait?
What did it say about the empty post?

tasks.task: Fix a typo in the post you just made. Then delete it.
tasks.done: The post is deleted.
questions: Where did you find edit?
Was there a time limit, and did you know about it before?
Did deleting ask you to confirm?

tasks.setup: Helper comments on the tester's post. At least 3 helpers open the post in the app and answer its question positively (questions are assigned on view; the free public line needs 3+ positive answers).
tasks.task: Find out how your post is doing: how many found it useful or interesting. If someone commented, pin the most helpful comment.
tasks.done: You've found whatever Skilient shows you, and pinned a comment.
questions: What did you find?
Why do you think there's no question under your own post?
Is it clear what Student Pro would add here? Would that be worth paying for?

tasks.setup: Tester has at least one friend and one venture chat; one tester with none
tasks.task: Send an interesting post to a friend with a short note. Then send another post to your venture's chat and undo it.
tasks.done: One post is sent and one is undone.
questions: Did you know whether your friend would be notified?
Did you notice Undo in time? Was it long enough?
Would you rather copy a link? Why?
(Testers with no chats yet) What did the share sheet tell you?

tasks.setup: Helper shares two posts in chat: one normal, and one university-only post at the tester's university that its author then deletes (to show the unavailable card).
tasks.task: Open the posts a friend sent you in chat. Then share several posts quickly to five chats in a row.
tasks.done: You've opened both shared posts and seen what happens when you share a lot.
questions: Could you tell a shared post apart from a normal message?
What did the unavailable post tell you?
What happened when you shared many posts fast?

tasks.task: Add two classmates as friends: one whose username you know, and one from Skilient's suggestions. Remove a suggestion for someone you don't know. Mistype one username on purpose.
tasks.done: Two requests are sent and one suggestion is gone.
questions: Why did Skilient suggest each person? Did the reason make sense?
What happened when you mistyped a username?
Where can you see the requests you've sent?

tasks.setup: Helper sends the tester a request; the tester has one unanswered outgoing request
tasks.task: A helper has sent you a friend request, and you've sent one that nobody answered. Accept the first and cancel yours. Then try adding the helper again.
tasks.done: You're friends with the helper and your other request is cancelled.
questions: How did you learn about the incoming request?
Were Received and Sent easy to tell apart?
What happened when you tried to add someone who's already your friend?

tasks.task: Message one of your friends starting from the Friends page. Then remove a friend you added by mistake.
tasks.done: You've sent a message and removed one friend.
questions: Where did you look for a way to message?
Was it too easy to remove a friend by accident?
What do you think the person loses when you remove them?

tasks.task: Someone (the helper account) is bothering you. Make sure they can't contact you or see you. Then undo it.
tasks.done: The helper is blocked and then unblocked.
questions: Where did you look first?
Did the confirmation explain what blocking does?
Could you undo it easily? Do you think they'd know?

tasks.setup: Helper is the tester's friend and replies during the session
tasks.task: Ask a friend (the helper) a question in chat and send a photo of your notes. Reply directly to their answer, react to it, then delete one of your messages.
tasks.done: The conversation is done.
questions: How could you tell your message was delivered?
Did your reply show which message it answered?
What did the deleted message look like afterwards?
What do you expect from WhatsApp that's missing here?

tasks.task: Turn on airplane mode, send a message, then turn the connection back on.
tasks.done: Your message has been sent.
questions: What did Skilient show while you were offline?
Did your message send by itself, or did you have to retry?
Did you ever think a message was sent when it wasn't?

tasks.task: Find an old message that mentioned a date, without scrolling. Then mute your venture chat and turn off read receipts.
tasks.done: You've found the message, muted the chat and turned receipts off.
questions: Where did you search?
What do you expect muting to change?
What changes for the other person when you turn off read receipts?

tasks.setup: Helper sends a '[UX test]' message to the tester
tasks.task: Try to message someone who isn't your friend: find Danish Helper in Explore. Then report a message from the helper marked '[UX test]'.
tasks.done: You know why you couldn't message them, and the message is reported.
questions: What stopped you, and did it say how you could message them?
Is that rule fair?
How sure were you that the right message got reported?
Do you have a chat called 'Deleted account'? What do you think it is?

tasks.task: Find a student at your university, in your batch, who has proved React skills. Look at their profile.
tasks.done: You're on a matching student's profile.
questions: How did you narrow the results?
Could you tell which skills were proved by code and which were only claimed?
What on the profile made you trust, or doubt, their skills?

tasks.task: Search for a name that doesn't exist with three filters on. Then open the profile of someone who isn't your friend.
tasks.done: You've seen the empty result and a stranger's profile.
questions: What did the empty result suggest?
What could you see on the stranger's profile? Did it explain why some was hidden?
Which actions could you take?

tasks.setup: Tester blocked someone in an earlier task (or blocks the helper now)
tasks.task: Look at your own profile the way others see it. Then search for the person you blocked earlier.
tasks.done: You've checked your profile and the search.
questions: How did you check what others see?
Was anything on your profile public that you didn't expect?
Your tier shows on your profile. How do you feel about that?

tasks.setup: Helper triggers a mix: chat messages, a friend request, a venture decision
tasks.task: Check what happened on Skilient since your last visit. Open the most important thing, then clear the rest.
tasks.done: Everything is marked read.
questions: Which notification mattered most? Was it easy to spot?
Were any notifications repeats of something you'd seen elsewhere, like chat?
Where did tapping one take you?
(New accounts) What did the empty page say?

tasks.task: Make Skilient email you only about requests and applications. Then get event reminders on your phone.
tasks.done: Email and phone notifications are set the way you want.
questions: How many settings did you have to change?
Were the categories named in words you'd use?
What did your browser ask you? Did you trust it?
notes: Push needs VAPID keys, the notify worker and a real phone.

tasks.task: Add Skilient to your phone's home screen and open it from there.
tasks.done: Skilient opens from your home screen.
questions: Did Skilient tell you this was possible?
Did it look and feel like an app?
Would you keep it on your home screen?
notes: Android Chrome install prompt, or iOS Share > Add to Home Screen; headless browsers can't.

tasks.setup: Helper venture with 2 open roles and 1 applicant question
tasks.task: Find a project at your university that needs someone with your skills, and apply for a role, explaining why you fit.
tasks.done: Your application is sent.
questions: How did you decide which role fit you?
What does '1 of 1 place open' mean to you?
After applying, where would you check how it's going?
Who did you think would read your message?
notes: Acceptance is checked in T048; look at the bell first, not the venture page.

tasks.setup: Helper accepts the tester's application during the session
tasks.task: The owner (helper) accepted you. Find your new team's chat and say hello. Then follow a different public venture.
tasks.done: You've posted in the team chat and followed another venture.
questions: How did you learn you were accepted?
What changed on the venture page now you're a member? Could you see every tab on your phone?
What does following a venture do?
notes: In the pilot the venture page changed before any notification was seen; ask testers which they noticed first.

tasks.setup: Helper sends an invite and declines a pending application
tasks.task: A helper invited you to a venture and declined another application of yours. Respond to the invite, then try applying again to the role that declined you.
tasks.done: You've answered the invite and seen what happens on re-applying.
questions: Where did you find the invite?
How did the decline message make you feel?
What happened when you tried to apply again?

tasks.setup: A full helper venture, and a university-only venture at another university if one exists
tasks.task: Try to join a venture that's full, and a university-only venture from another university.
tasks.done: You've seen why you can't join either.
questions: Did the page say why before you tapped anything?
Did it suggest anything else to do?

tasks.task: Start a project called '[UX test] <your name>' looking for a designer and a backend developer, visible only to your university, with one question for applicants. Submit once with the title empty first.
tasks.done: Your venture exists with two roles and a question.
questions: Which fields were unclear?
On the manage page, did you always know whether your changes were saved? Did you lose anything?
How long did set-up take? Was anything asked twice?

tasks.task: Announce your project in the feed so students can apply.
tasks.done: An invite post for your venture is in the feed.
questions: How did you link the post to your venture?
How does the post look to others? How did you check?
Did you know you could do this from Home?

tasks.setup: Two helpers apply to the tester's venture
tasks.task: Two people applied (helpers). Read their applications, accept one and decline the other. Then invite a classmate by username.
tasks.done: One applicant is in, one is declined and an invite is sent.
questions: Did you have enough information to decide?
What happened to the application chat after you accepted?
Did the declined person get a reason? Should they?

tasks.task: Your team has started work. Mark the venture as in progress, post a progress update, link your GitHub repository and add a deliverable link.
tasks.done: The venture is In progress with an update and a deliverable.
questions: What does 'Start building' mean to you? Can it be undone?
Where do updates appear for other people?
What's the difference between an update and a deliverable?

tasks.setup: Tester's venture has the helper as a member
tasks.task: Give a teammate the role 'Designer', then make the helper the venture's owner.
tasks.done: The helper owns the venture.
questions: Did transferring ownership ask you to confirm and explain what you lose?
Could you get ownership back?

tasks.setup: Venture with the helper as a member and contributions to confirm
tasks.task: Try to complete your venture now. If Skilient stops you, find out what's needed and do it.
tasks.done: The venture is Completed.
questions: Did the message say exactly what was missing?
How did completing feel?
Where did the finished venture show up afterwards?

tasks.task: Abandon a test venture you no longer need.
tasks.done: The venture is abandoned.
questions: Did the confirmation explain what happens?
Can it be undone?

tasks.task: Record what you did for your team this week, with a link as evidence (try a bad link first). Then confirm a teammate's entry.
tasks.done: Your entry is logged and a teammate's is confirmed.
questions: In your words, what's the difference between 'self-reported' and 'peer-verified'?
Was it clear you can't edit an entry later?
Did anything make you hesitate before confirming someone else's work?

tasks.task: You made a mistake in your entry. Fix it.
tasks.done: A correction is logged.
questions: How did you fix it?
Did you understand why you can't edit it?
What would you do after 24 hours?

tasks.setup: Completed venture with the helper; helper endorses the tester
tasks.task: Your venture is complete. Endorse each teammate for skills you saw them use. Then hide one endorsement you received and look at the Reviews tab.
tasks.done: Endorsements are given and one is hidden.
questions: How did you choose skills? Was the limit of 5 fine?
What do you think an endorsement adds to their profile?
Why might someone hide an endorsement?
What is the Reviews tab for?

tasks.task: Update your profile: new photo, a one-line bio and what you're looking for. Make your full profile visible only to people at your university. Try leaving the page before saving once.
tasks.done: Your profile shows the changes.
questions: Did you know when it was saved?
Which visibility option did you pick, and what do you think others now see?
Were there settings you expected but didn't find?

tasks.setup: Any signed-in tester who has already done T079 (or reset the leaderboard opt-out after this task)
tasks.task: Make sure you don't appear on leaderboards. Then check who has viewed your CV.
tasks.done: You're off the leaderboards and you've seen your CV views.
questions: How long did it take to find these settings?
The page mentions recruiters. What do you think that means right now?
Was anything on this page confusing?

tasks.task: Check which devices are signed into your account and sign out of all devices. Then sign in again and sign out here, with Skilient open in two tabs.
tasks.done: You're signed out everywhere.
questions: Could you recognise your devices in the list?
What made you trust it worked?
What happened in the other tab?

tasks.task: Find what data Skilient keeps about you and how to delete your account. Start deleting it, then cancel.
tasks.done: Deletion is cancelled and your account still works.
questions: Was it clear what happens to your Record, CV and ventures?
How did you cancel? Did you feel safe?
Was the privacy notice easy to read?

tasks.setup: Staff approve or reject within the session (one rejection with a reason)
tasks.task: Add a certificate you've earned (for example a course certificate PDF). Try a file that's too big first. Then check where it appears.
tasks.done: The certificate is approved, or you know what to fix.
questions: Did you know who reviews it and how long it takes?
What did each status mean?
Where did it appear once approved?

tasks.task: Find out what Student Pro gives you, whether you have it now, and what happens when the beta ends.
tasks.done: You can answer all three.
questions: In one sentence, what does Pro add?
Do you have it now? How do you know?
Does anything feel like paying for a better rank?

tasks.task: Something on Skilient confused you today. Tell the team, with a screenshot. Check back later for a reply.
tasks.done: Your feedback shows a status or a reply.
questions: Where did you look for a way to give feedback?
Did you know what would happen next?
Would you check 'My feedback' again later?

tasks.setup: Staff remove a '[UX test]' post and restrict a test account, then decide the appeal
tasks.task: Staff removed one of your test posts and restricted your test account. Find out why, and appeal one of the two decisions.
tasks.done: Your appeal of one decision has an outcome.
questions: Was the reason specific enough?
Was the appeal easy to find?
Did the outcome feel fair, whatever it was?

tasks.task: Look at your skills. Pick one and find out exactly why it has its level and what you'd need to do to reach the next level.
tasks.done: You can explain one skill's level.
questions: In your words, what does L2 mean?
Could you tell which skills came from code and which you claimed?
Is the next-level advice something you could do this week?

tasks.task: Add a skill Skilient hasn't detected (for example public speaking). Then stop Skilient reading one of your repositories.
tasks.done: The claimed skill is added and one repository is excluded.
questions: What happens to a claimed skill?
Was it clear what excluding a repository changes?
What do you think would happen to your skills if you disconnected GitHub?

tasks.setup: Tester who skipped GitHub in onboarding
tasks.task: (If you skipped GitHub during set-up) Connect GitHub now from Settings. Cancel once on GitHub's page, then do it properly.
tasks.done: Your repositories are syncing or synced.
questions: Did GitHub's page match what Skilient said would happen?
How long did the sync take, and did you know it was working?
Where did you end up after cancelling?
notes: Needs the GitHub App and the github-worker.

tasks.task: You want to become a backend developer. Find what you should learn next and why. Then try following three paths.
tasks.done: You know your next skill and why.
questions: What's a 'Starter path'? Did you trust the order?
What does the ladder tell you at a glance?
What happened with the third path?

tasks.task: Start a proof task for your next skill and submit it with one of your repositories.
tasks.done: The task is done, or waiting for a reviewer.
questions: Was the checklist clear enough to do without asking anyone?
After submitting, did you know what was happening and how long it would take?
When it finished, what changed?
notes: The GitHub check is worker-driven; allow tasks.limits github_wait_minutes before judging the wait.

tasks.setup: Helper reviewer marks the task 'Needs changes'
tasks.task: Your task came back with 'Needs changes'. Fix it and resubmit.
tasks.done: The task is resubmitted.
questions: Was the reviewer's note clear enough to act on?
How did you resubmit?
Would you rather take a code check instead? Why?
notes: Peer routing runs on the proof-tasks-tick cron.

tasks.setup: Tester has L2 in a skill; helper submits a task in that skill
tasks.task: A student asked you to review their proof task. Review it fairly.
tasks.done: You've confirmed it, asked for changes or declined.
questions: What did 'checking' mean to you: run the code, read it, or something else?
Was the checklist enough to decide?
Reviewers get no Record entry. Is that fair?
How would you decline?
notes: Peer routing runs on the proof-tasks-tick cron.

tasks.task: You want to learn SQL from a senior. Find someone who can teach you and send a request with two times that suit you.
tasks.done: Your request is sent.
questions: What made you pick that teacher?
Was it clear what you'd owe in return?
If nobody was listed, what did Skilient suggest?

tasks.setup: Two testers paired; one has a skill at L2+
tasks.task: Pair up: one of you teaches, one learns. Accept the request, agree a session time, meet for 15 minutes, then confirm it happened and close the swap.
tasks.done: The teacher has a 'Taught' entry on their Record.
questions: How did you agree on a time?
(Learner) Was 'Did your session happen?' easy to answer honestly?
(Teacher) Where did your Taught entry appear?
What would stop you from doing this again?

tasks.task: Find out why your score is what it is, and the single best thing you could do this month to raise it.
tasks.done: You can name one action.
questions: Explain your score in one sentence.
Did the dates make sense (for example 'updated …')?
Did anything feel unfair or easy to game?

tasks.setup: Any signed-in tester; run before T062 (which opts out of leaderboards)
tasks.task: See where you stand in your department and batch, then across all universities.
tasks.done: You've seen both boards.
questions: How did you feel seeing your position?
You can't see other people's points. Is that good?
Would you opt out? Why?

tasks.setup: Tester has at least 2 entries (from a test event or swap)
tasks.task: Look at your Record. Pin your best entry to your profile, download its certificate, and check it at its verify link.
tasks.done: You've seen the entry's verify page.
questions: What does 'Sealed' mean to you?
Would a scholarship committee trust this certificate? Why?
Was the verify page convincing?

tasks.task: Share your whole Record with a scholarship committee for one week only, and download the transcript. Then cancel the link.
tasks.done: The link is revoked and you have the transcript PDF.
questions: How did you set it to last a week?
Was it clear what the link shows (hidden entries too?)
Did revoking feel final?

tasks.setup: Officer helper corrects one entry and revokes another
tasks.task: One of your entries has a mistake. Get it fixed.
tasks.done: The corrected entry is on your Record.
questions: Who did you think would fix it?
What happened to the old entry?
(If an entry was revoked) Was the reason enough? How would you appeal?

tasks.task: Open your Record before you've attended any event.
tasks.done: You know how you'd get a first entry.
questions: Is it clear how to get your first entry?
Does the suggested next step make sense to you?

tasks.setup: Tester on a Pro trial (on the free plan CV changes apply at the next monthly refresh)
tasks.task: Get your CV ready for an internship application: hide sections you don't want, put projects first, and include one society activity.
tasks.done: Your CV shows what you chose.
questions: Was it clear you can't type things into this CV? Is that good or bad?
Is anything printed that you'd rather not show (for example your tier)?
Would you send this CV as it is?

tasks.task: Send your CV to an employer as a link that expires in 30 days, and as a PDF. Then check whether anyone has opened your links.
tasks.done: You have a link and a PDF, or you know why not.
questions: What stopped you, if anything, and did it explain why?
Is the line between free and Pro clear and fair?
Where did you see who opened your link?

tasks.setup: Helper on a Pro trial exports one genuine CV PDF, and prints a copy with a single character changed
tasks.task: A classmate sent you two copies of their Skilient CV PDF. Check whether each one is genuine.
tasks.done: You know which copy is genuine.
questions: How did you check?
What did the page say for the edited copy? Was it clear?
Would you trust this more than a normal CV?

tasks.task: You have a free afternoon this week. Use Skilient to find something worth joining or applying to.
tasks.done: You've opened one opening's page.
questions: Which card did you open first, and why?
Did the page feel full or empty? What did empty cards suggest?
How did you know what's new since your last visit?

tasks.setup: A faculty helper posts a project idea. Tester hasn't created a venture today (daily create limit).
tasks.task: Find a project idea from a teacher, filter and sort the list, and start a venture on the idea you like.
tasks.done: A venture based on the idea exists, or you know why not.
questions: Was it clear who posted the idea and what they expect?
Did filtering and sorting help?
What would you do next?

tasks.setup: Three test societies with Open, By request and Inductions only modes
tasks.task: Find a society you'd like to hear from. Follow it, then become a member of two societies.
tasks.done: You follow one and are a member (or pending) in two.
questions: What's the difference between following and being a member?
On a society page, what do 'Following' and 'Leave' mean? Did you press one by mistake?
When you asked to join, did you know what happens next?

tasks.setup: Officer helper opens a round and accepts or declines during the session
tasks.task: A society is recruiting for its design team. Apply.
tasks.done: Your application is sent and later decided.
questions: Were the deadline and number of seats clear?
After applying, where would you check?
How did you hear the result?

tasks.setup: Officer helper posts a '[UX test]' society post
tasks.task: Leave a society you joined by mistake, and report the society post titled '[UX test]'.
tasks.done: You've left one society and reported the post.
questions: Did leaving warn you about anything you'd lose?
Did the report reasons fit?
(If your university has no societies) What did Skilient suggest?

tasks.task: You're an office bearer of a society that isn't on Skilient. Request it (name it '[UX test] …'). Try an existing society's name first, and try sending a second request afterwards.
tasks.done: Your request says Pending.
questions: Did you have the proof it asked for? What would you use in real life?
Which step took longest?
After submitting, what did you expect, and when?

tasks.setup: Staff ask for more info, then approve one request and reject another
tasks.task: Staff asked for more information about your society request. Fix it and resubmit, then check the final decision.
tasks.done: Your society is live, or you know why not.
questions: Was the staff request clear?
When it was approved, did you know what to do first?
(If rejected) Was the reason fair?

tasks.setup: Officer helper publishes a free workshop with a 2-question form
tasks.task: Find an upcoming workshop at your university and register as a participant. Get your ticket ready for the door.
tasks.done: Your ticket is on screen.
questions: Before registering, what did you think you'd get from attending?
Was the form short enough?
How would you find your ticket on the day with no internet?

tasks.task: Register for a hackathon as a team of three: one of you creates the team, the others join with its code.
tasks.done: All three are registered as one team.
questions: How did you share the team code?
Did everyone know they were registered?
What do you think happens if a teammate cancels?

tasks.setup: Four helper events set up in those states
tasks.task: Try to register for an event that's full, one for another batch only, one whose registration hasn't opened, and one that was cancelled. Join the waitlist for the full one.
tasks.done: You're on the waitlist and know why you can't join the others.
questions: Did each page say why before you pressed anything?
Did you know your waitlist position and what happens next?
Did you hit any dead end?

tasks.setup: Run together with the officer check-in session (S11)
tasks.task: On the day: get reminded, get checked in at the door with your ticket, and fill in the feedback form afterwards.
tasks.done: Your Record shows the new entry.
questions: Did you get the reminders? Where?
Did the QR scan first time? Did you notice the brightness hint?
How did it feel when the Record entry arrived?
notes: Reminders need the notify worker; the door check-in is S11's officer.

tasks.task: You can't make it anymore. Cancel your registration.
tasks.done: Your registration is cancelled.
questions: Was cancelling easy to find?
Did it tell you what happens to your seat or any refund?

tasks.setup: Test society with confirmed payment details; the team refunds the PKR 100 afterwards
tasks.task: Buy a PKR 100 ticket to the test society's paid event. Pay the society, upload your receipt, and wait for confirmation.
tasks.done: Your paid ticket is confirmed.
questions: Before paying, did you trust the payment details? What made you trust or doubt them?
Did you know where to put the reference code?
While it was under review, did you know your seat was safe?
How long did approval take, and how were you told?

tasks.setup: Officer helper rejects the first receipt, then approves; refund policy allows cancelling
tasks.task: Your receipt was rejected. Upload the right one. Then cancel and get your refund.
tasks.done: You've marked the refund as received (or not).
questions: Was the rejection reason enough to fix it?
Who did you think was responsible for the refund: Skilient or the society?
Did you know what to do if the refund never arrived? Or if you never uploaded a receipt?

tasks.setup: Approved test society; helper officer and a helper join request
tasks.task: Your society is live. Finish its set-up: add a logo, invite a co-officer (helper) as General Secretary for this academic year (type the dates: 1 September to 30 June), choose how students join, and handle a join request.
tasks.done: The checklist is done and the co-officer is on the roll call.
questions: Did the checklist make the order obvious?
Was 'term' (start and end month) clear?
Which membership mode did you choose, and did the page explain the trade-off?

tasks.task: Post an announcement as your society, not as yourself.
tasks.done: A post with your society's name is in the feed.
questions: How did you switch between posting as yourself and as the society?
How did you check what students see?

tasks.task: Set up how students pay your society for tickets (use a test JazzCash number). Your co-officer must confirm it.
tasks.done: The payment details are confirmed and live.
questions: Did you understand why a second officer has to confirm?
While waiting, could you tell the details weren't live yet?
(Co-officer) What would you check before confirming?

tasks.setup: Test officers' term end date set in the past; staff can suspend a test society to show that state
tasks.task: It's the end of term. Hand the presidency to your co-officer, then check that the new President can confirm your officers' terms.
tasks.done: Your co-officer is President and your officers' terms are confirmed or waiting for them.
questions: Did you know confirming a term issues a Record entry?
Did the handover warn you it can't be undone?
How will you know your own term was confirmed?

tasks.task: Recruit 2 designers and 1 writer for your society, with one question for applicants, closing in a week. Try a deadline two months away first.
tasks.done: The round is published.
questions: Was anything about roles or seats confusing?
How did you check what students see?
Did you know who would be notified when you published?

tasks.task: Three students applied (helpers). Shortlist two, accept one and decline one with a kind note.
tasks.done: One applicant is accepted and one declined.
questions: Could you compare applicants easily on your phone?
Did you know what the declined student would see?
What happens to the applicant you didn't decide on?

tasks.task: Create a two-session React workshop for BSCS students only, 40 seats, free, with one form question. People who attend both sessions should earn 'Completed'. Save it as a draft first, then publish.
tasks.done: The event is published.
questions: Which step took longest, and why?
Did 'N steps left' help?
Was the Record step (what attendees earn) clear?
Did you skip something you later needed?

tasks.setup: Society with and without confirmed payment details
tasks.task: Add a paid PKR 200 'Participant' ticket and a free 'Audience' ticket to an event, with refunds allowed until 2 days before. Invite another society to co-host. Then duplicate a past event.
tasks.done: Both tickets are set and a duplicate exists.
questions: Did you understand that Skilient doesn't handle the money?
Was the refund policy wording clear?
Did duplicating copy what you expected?

tasks.setup: Helpers register; one uploads the same receipt twice
tasks.task: Five students registered, two of them paid. Review the payments: one receipt is a duplicate. Approve the valid ones and reject the other with a reason.
tasks.done: Every payment is decided.
questions: Could you check the amount and reference quickly?
Did the duplicate flag make sense?
Was the receipt readable on your phone?

tasks.setup: Manual-approval event with a pending registration
tasks.task: Approve a pending registration, add a volunteer as check-in staff, and tell everyone the venue changed. Try lowering capacity below the number registered.
tasks.done: Staff added and the change notice sent.
questions: Did you know registrants were told about the change?
What happened when you lowered capacity?
Is there anything you'd want to message to only some registrants?

tasks.task: Cancel a test event that has paid registrations.
tasks.done: The event shows Cancelled.
questions: Did it explain the consequences before you confirmed?
Was it clear the society refunds, not Skilient?

tasks.setup: Run with attendee testers from S09
tasks.task: At the door, check in five attendees: scan three tickets (one of them twice), find one person by name, and add a walk-in by university email. Deny camera access once.
tasks.done: Five people are checked in.
questions: Could you tell green, amber and red apart at arm's length, outdoors?
How fast was each check-in?
What did you do for the person without a ticket?
notes: Needs a camera (BarcodeDetector) for scanning and the colour question.

tasks.task: Use self check-in for a room: show the rotating code and have two people scan it. Turn off Wi-Fi once.
tasks.done: Both people are checked in.
questions: Did attendees know what to do?
Could people outside the room misuse it?
What happened when the connection dropped?
notes: Self check-in exists only for university events, not society events. Kept for the id; skip it until it's built.

tasks.task: Your event has ended. Add one attendee who was missed, enter 1st to 3rd place, log 2 volunteer hours (no more than the event's length) for a helper, and issue the entries. Include yourself as an attendee.
tasks.done: Entries are issued.
questions: Did the preview make you confident before issuing?
Was it clear issued entries can't be edited?
Did you know what happens if you don't close out?

tasks.task: An attendee reported a mistake in their entry. Correct it. Then download the attendee list and read the feedback summary.
tasks.done: The correction is issued and you have the CSV.
questions: Was it clear the old entry stays visible as 'Superseded'?
Did the CSV open correctly in your spreadsheet app?
Was the feedback summary useful?
